prompt:
A full-length figure of an enemy for the pre-fight screen of a mythology card game, made by hand like a 1993 fantasy trading-card or game-book illustration, exactly matching the game's painted backgrounds: bold, wobbly black pen-and-ink outlines around every shape, filled with thin, flat, transparent watercolour and gouache washes. Big simple flat shapes of colour with almost no shading or modelling, a little ink cross-hatching in the shadows, blotchy uneven washes with hard dried edges, splatters and visible brush marks, and the rough off-white paper texture and grain showing through the paint. Naive, slightly clumsy, decorative and stylised, like an old printed card with slightly faded, misregistered colour, in the limited palette given below. Absolutely not realistic: no realistic lighting or anatomy rendering, no glossy highlights, no glow, no soft gradients, no fine fur or skin detail, no oil-painting look, no 3D, no digital painting, not modern concept art or AI art. The body is seen in three-quarter view from slightly below, angled away from the viewer, but the head is turned and the eyes look straight at the viewer, sizing them up. A relaxed, casual, confident pose, at ease and completely sure of itself: standing or leaning with its weight on one leg, its weapon resting or held loosely, not attacking, not lunging, not shouting. Menace through calm. Give it depth and volume: overlapping forms and shading washes and ink hatching that model the body in light and shadow, lit by the light of its scene (given below), as if painted into the same picture as the backdrop; still hand-drawn, never glossy, airbrushed or rendered. Only a faint, soft, semi-transparent painted shadow on the ground under the feet; no smoke, mist, dust or embers anywhere. The whole figure fits inside the frame. Cut out cleanly on a fully transparent background apart from that shadow: no scenery, no moon, sun, fire or other light source drawn in (the backdrop already has it), no frame, no text. The flat bright colours and bold outlines of Egyptian tomb painting mixed into the pen-and-ink style.

Subject: Sekhmet, the lioness-headed Egyptian goddess of war and plague: a tall powerful woman with the head of a fierce lioness crowned by a blazing red sun disc and a rearing cobra, in a red linen dress and a broad collar of gold and lapis, standing in three-quarter profile with her weight on one hip, the sceptre held loosely at her side, head turned toward the viewer with a cool, predatory stare, mouth closed. Ancient Egyptian in every detail. Light: the blazing sun above and behind her, hot light along her edges.
Colour: blazing orange, red and gold (#2a0a04 to #e07a24) with black granite and white glare.
